### Observed differences

- Three activities that were absent from the earlier window — A32, A33 and A38 — each appear in about 50 in 100 traces in the later window (98–100 of 200 traces), positioned around the middle of the trace (median relative position about 0.5). [OCC031, OCC032, OCC037, POS007, POS008, POS009]
- The routing after A26 split: earlier, about 95 in 100 of A26's outgoing transitions went to A27, A27 ran in every trace and preceded A28 in about 98 in 100 of them; in the later window about 51 in 100 of A26's outgoing transitions go to A27 and about 49 in 100 go directly to A32, A33 or A38, and A27 appears in only about 52 in 100 traces. [DIR026, OCC026, REL027]
- The new activities behave as one cluster: any two of them co-occur in about 49 in 100 later-window traces and appear in both orders in similar shares (no fixed order among the three), each of the three can directly precede A28, and A27 co-occurs with any of them in only about 1–2 in 100 traces — they are near-perfect alternatives. [REL034, REL035, REL036, DIR032, DIR033, DIR038, REL028, REL029, REL030]
- The A26-to-A28 distance grew accordingly: earlier the pair was two steps apart in about 91 in 100 observations; later it is two steps apart in about 50 in 100 and four steps apart in about 46 in 100, as expected when three activities are inserted between them. [LAG011]
- A04 became far more prominent: it appears in about 60 in 100 traces (about 19 in 100 before) and much earlier in the trace (mean relative position about 0.21 versus 0.54); A14 now leads directly to A04 in about 54 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (about 4 in 100 before), A04 leads to A15 in about 87 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (previously spread over many successors), and A14 is immediately followed by A04 in about 96 in 100 of the later observations of that pair. [OCC004, POS001, DIR014, DIR004, LAG005]
- A02, A06 and A08 appear in fewer traces (roughly from 16, 20 and 16 in 100 down to about 8, 4 and 8 in 100); each of these rests on only 8–16 later-window traces and is therefore weakly supported. [OCC002, OCC006, OCC008]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that a new alternative segment was inserted between A26 and A28: in the later window, about half of the traces replace the former chain A26 → A27 → A28 with A26 followed by the three new activities A32, A33 and A38 — executed together in varying order — before reaching A28, so that A27 is bypassed in about 49 in 100 traces although it still precedes A28 whenever it runs. The signs are direct and consistent: A26's outgoing transitions shifted from about 95 in 100 towards A27 to a roughly 51/49 split between A27 and the new activities, A27 and the new activities are nearly mutually exclusive, A28 now occurs without A27 in about 49 in 100 traces (never earlier), and the A26–A28 lag moved from two to four steps in about half the observations, while the new activities rose from 0 to about 50 in 100 traces — differences larger than those seen in about 99 in 100 random re-splits of the pooled windows. [DIR026, REL027, REL028, REL029, REL030, LAG011, OCC026, OCC031, OCC032, OCC037]

The evidence shows which edges are taken and how often, but not why a trace takes one branch or the other; and zero participation earlier means only that A32, A33 and A38 were not observed before, so a very low-frequency presence in the earlier window cannot be ruled out. [OCC031, OCC032, OCC037]

Other differences: A04 now runs between A14 and A15 in roughly half of the traces — A14 leads directly to A04 in about 54 in 100 of its outgoing transitions and A04 leads to A15 in about 87 in 100, with the A14-to-A15 distance shifting from one to two steps accordingly — whereas earlier A14 led almost always straight to A15 and A04 was rare and late in the trace; this second insertion-like change is directly supported but is kept separate from the main hypothesis. [OCC004, POS001, DIR014, DIR004, LAG005, LAG006, REL001, REL002, REL003] The lower participation of A02, A06 and A08 is noted above but rests on few later-window observations. [OCC002, OCC006, OCC008]
